explanation: The first sentence explains that the richest gold was buried deep in rock, out of reach of individual prospectors. Giving up and going to work for large mining companies is a result of that fact, so "Consequently" fits. "Still" would wrongly signal a contrast with the previous sentence.

The text moves in time order: Gomez won a competition in 2014 and then, in 2017, created his own show. "Later" marks this sequence. "For example" fails because creating the show is not an example of winning the competition.

The text describes a process: the user "first" tags the photo, and after that the software analyzes facial features and looks for matches. "Then" signals the next step. "For example" is wrong because the analysis is not an example of tagging.

The first sentence says Thaden was "already" a record breaker when she won the August 1929 race, and the next sentence describes a record she set in December 1928, before that race. "Earlier" signals this step back in time. "Next" wrongly suggests the record came after the race.

Butterflies with bold, brightly colored wings are being contrasted with species whose wings are nearly colorless and transparent. "However" signals that contrast. "Similarly" fails because the two kinds of wings are opposites, not alike.

Choice B describes the specific work: when it is expanded it shows a panoramic landscape painted in ink and watercolor, and it doesn't stop to explain what a leporello is, which suits readers who already know. Choices A and D spend words defining leporellos, which this audience doesn't need, and C barely describes the work at all.

Painting #12 is even-numbered, and the notes say even-numbered paintings are at the Museum of Modern Art in New York City, so A gives the right place. Choice C wrongly sends readers to Washington, DC, where the odd-numbered paintings are, and D names both places without saying which one has Painting #12.

The mother has lost sight of her calf and wants to be sure it is safe, and that is the reason she gives an infrasonic call. "For this reason" shows this cause-and-effect link. "For example" fails because the call is a response to the situation, not an example of it.

Choice A names a similarity between CTAB 2X and Pplant (both fell short on yield or purity) and explains why it matters: for that reason the researchers judged both less effective than Pbact. Choice C states a similarity but not why it is significant. Choice D is factually wrong, since CTAB 2X (2.2) and Pbact (1.6) had different purity ratios.

Choice B directly contrasts the two ("Unlike traditional biennials") and names what is different: the MexiCali Biennial uses different venues and an uneven schedule. Choice C describes only traditional biennials and never mentions the MexiCali Biennial, and A and D give facts without drawing a contrast.

The text compares two months to show how much sunspot numbers vary: about 180 sunspots in one month and only about 2 in another. "By comparison" introduces the second number as a point of contrast. "Similarly" fails because the two numbers are very different.

Because the audio gets more distorted as carbon levels rise, listeners can hear those changes. That is a result, so "thus" fits. "For instance" is wrong because hearing the changes is a consequence of the distortion, not an example of it.

The text contrasts lower elevations, where snowpack peaked in early March, with higher elevations, where it peaked in mid-March. "On the other hand" signals that contrast. "In other words" fails because the second finding is different from the first, not a restatement of it.
The goal is to give the green iguana's average length, and only B does that: 4.8 feet. The other choices talk about where the iguana lives or what it eats, which doesn't meet the goal.

To introduce the movement to new readers, A names it, says when it was founded, and sums up its main goals: access to healthy food, sustainable production, and fair treatment of workers. Choice D says "the movement" without naming it, C is too narrow, and B gives only founding dates without saying what the movement stands for.

Choice A clearly says that Mary Ann Evans was the real author and that George Eliot was her pseudonym. Choice D mentions a woman who revealed herself as the author but never gives her name, so it doesn't actually identify her.

Choice B shows the effect of media by contrasting before and after: Wong Fei-hung was known only locally in his lifetime, but later films and TV turned him into an international folk hero. Choice A gets the cause wrong, since his local fame as a physician came from his own life, not from media, and C and D mention media without showing what it did to his legacy.

Choice B gives the study's purpose (to understand how ducklings save energy) and its method: Yuan used computer simulations of the mother duck's wake. Choices A and D focus on the results and never mention the computer simulations, so they leave out the methodology.

The first sentence admits that Morton exaggerated when he claimed to have invented jazz, and the second says that he still shaped the genre. "Though" signals this contrasting point. "Therefore" fails because his real influence does not follow from his exaggeration.
Niger ratified the treaty, but Jordan has only signed it and not ratified it. "In contrast" marks this difference. "Similarly" fails because the two countries did different things.

The text lists Brunning's reasons in order. The first reason is introduced with "First," so the second reason, about the huge effort needed to bury the ship, should begin with "Second." "Instead" and "Still" wrongly suggest a contrast between the two reasons, which actually support the same conclusion.

The words after the blank define the term "cognate replacement": it is the rate at which a word gets replaced over time by a noncognate form. "That is" introduces a definition or restatement. "For example" fails because the phrase explains the term rather than giving an example of it.

The notes say that both inventions improved on existing designs, and A states this shared feature directly with "both." Choice C focuses on how the inventions differ, and B and D each describe only one invention.

The first sentence makes a general claim about surprising adaptations that help organisms survive harsh conditions, and tadpole shrimp embryos pausing development during drought are one such adaptation. "For example" introduces this specific case. "In contrast" fails because the example supports the claim instead of opposing it.

In most plants ABA slows processes down, but in S. parvula it speeds growth up. "In contrast" signals this opposite result. "For example" fails because S. parvula is an exception to the general pattern, not an example of it.

The glaciers are at least 60 million years old, and the ice sheet formed 34 million years ago, so the researchers concluded that glaciers existed long before the ice sheet. That conclusion follows from the evidence, so "Thus" fits. "Nevertheless" and "Even so" wrongly signal that the conclusion goes against the evidence.

The civil war made it hard for Amaya to perform in Spain, and because of that she left to perform abroad. "As a result" shows this cause and effect. "For example" fails because leaving Spain is a consequence of the war, not an example of it.

An overview should sum up the main findings: syllable rates differed across languages, but information rates were about the same for all 17. Choice D says exactly that. Choice A gives only what was measured, not the findings, and B and C wrongly say that one language conveyed information faster than the other.

Choice C compares what each woman did at the march: Hedgeman worked behind the scenes to make sure a woman would speak, and Bates was the woman who spoke. Choice A describes only Bates's contribution, and B compares their careers rather than their roles at the march.

Because companies own and sell breathable air in this alternate Nigeria, people have to buy it with O2 credits. That is a direct result, so "As a result" fits. "Nevertheless" would wrongly suggest that buying air goes against what came before.

A seal must save energy and oxygen on a deep dive, and that is why it moves its flippers as little as possible and glides. "For this reason" signals this cause-and-effect link. "On the other hand" fails because gliding is a response to the challenge, not a contrast with it.

The text lists ways Idár fought injustice. Founding the League of Mexican Women is a second action added to her work as a reporter, so "Additionally" fits. "For example" fails because founding the league is not an example of her newspaper writing.

Slow blinks went with shorter talking times, while quick blinks went with longer talking times. "By contrast" signals this opposite result. "Specifically" fails because the second finding doesn't add detail to the first; it describes the opposite case.

The text describes the machine's steps in order: "first" it scraped the ice, then it sprayed water, and "lastly" it smoothed the ice. "Next" marks the middle step. "Similarly" and "In contrast" don't show sequence.

Choice B gives the exact founding year and says that the museum "has served" the Pueblo "since 1992," which highlights how long it has existed. Choice C hints at the date ("the 1990s") only in parentheses while focusing on the mission, and A and D give no date at all.

The text first praises the book's vivid prose and then adds a second strength: its many high-quality images. "Additionally" signals that something is being added. "Consequently" fails because the images are not a result of the writing.
Choice A names what P waves and S waves share: both travel beneath Earth's surface and both make the ground move. Choices B and D focus on differences, and C describes only P waves.
The text lists three steps, introduced by "First" and "Third," so the missing middle step should start with "Second." The other choices don't fit the numbered sequence.

Choice B explains the term (a mix of "flora" and "fauna" used for plant-animal hybrids) and gives a concrete example: a parrot with leaves for feathers. Choice A explains the word but gives no example, and C and D name paintings without saying what they show or what the term means.

Choice B uses one poem, "Towards Autumn," and shows how it follows the sestina form: thirty-nine lines and six end words, listed correctly, that alternate in a set pattern. Choice A mentions both poems without giving details, and C and D pair the poems with the wrong sets of end words.

The text first describes Paris as an ideal place for Sher-Gil, where she was learning and building a name. Even so, she longed to go back to India, which goes against what you might expect, so "Still" fits. "Therefore" fails because wanting to leave does not follow from Paris being ideal.

The reason the Pleiades looks different is that two of its stars moved so close together that they now look like one, and C states this cause. Choice B describes the change but not why it happened. Choice D wrongly suggests that the two stars have always been that close.

For readers who don't know Kahlo, D gives a useful introduction: who she was (an influential twentieth-century Mexican painter) and what she is best known for (vivid, symbolic self-portraits). The other choices jump straight to a particular painting without first explaining who Kahlo is.

Choice D contrasts the two methods: Rai uses a natural, plant-based substance where manufacturers have traditionally used hazardous chemicals. Choice A points out a similarity (both dyes use indigo), and B and C each describe only one side.

The aim of the study was to find out how ocean temperature affects where blue whales forage for krill, and B states that goal ("sought to determine"). Choices A and C report what the study found, not what it set out to learn.

The researchers built computer models, and the T. rex size estimate in the second sentence came from those models. "Based on these models" shows that link. "Despite these estimates" wrongly suggests that the conclusion goes against the models.

Choice A introduces both the author and the novel: it names Selvon and says he was Trinidadian, and it gives the novel's title, its publication year, and what it is about. Choice C never names Selvon, and B and D focus on a different novel without explaining what either book is about.
Choice C points out something the two species share: both live in the Atlantic Ocean. Choices B and D stress how the species differ, and A mentions only the olive ridley sea turtle.

The text describes a chain of causes: the moving metals create electrical currents, and those currents then create a protective barrier. "In turn" signals the next link in a chain of effects. "Likewise" fails because the second step isn't being compared to the first, and "nevertheless" wrongly signals a contrast.

After listing Copeland's impressive achievements, the text says that none of them matches the honor of becoming principal dancer. That shift calls for a contrast word, so "However" fits. "For example" fails because the last sentence isn't another item on the list; it sets one honor above all the others.

Core differentiation alone would leave the upper mantle short of siderophiles, but there are far more siderophiles than that model predicts. So the extra siderophiles must have come from somewhere else, such as asteroid or comet impacts. This conclusion follows from the evidence, so "Hence" fits. "That said" would wrongly signal a contrast.

The text describes two actions in time order: a court victory in January and an open letter in April. "Later" shows that the second action came after the first. "For instance" fails because the letter is not an example of the court case.

Dillard struggles throughout the book to reconcile nature's beauty and its harshness, and in the end she sees them as inseparable. "Ultimately" signals this final conclusion that the struggle leads to. "Moreover" fails because the last sentence doesn't just add another point; it describes where her struggle ends up.

The goal is a similarity in age, and A notes that both malls are very old: Qianmen Dajie dates back to the Ming dynasty, and "likewise" Rue Mouffetard has existed for centuries. Choices B and C give similarities that have nothing to do with age, and D wrongly suggests that the malls are from the 19th or 20th century.

Choice C makes a claim (Tharpe had a major impact on rock 'n' roll) and backs it up with a direct quotation from Henderson calling her its "founding mother." Choice B paraphrases Henderson instead of quoting her, and D quotes Moore about Tharpe's singing, not about rock 'n' roll.

Choice D makes a general claim about exoplanets (their names come from many different sources) and supports it with two examples: one name from Greek mythology and one from Malay. Choice B only compares two planets without generalizing, and C generalizes about stars, not exoplanets.

Choice D uses "whereas" to contrast why each animal glows: jellyfish do it to startle predators, while black dragonfish do it to find prey. Choice A focuses on what the two have in common, and B describes only the dragonfish.

Larlarb usually custom fits costumes to each actor, but for Sunshine she had spacesuits made in a few standard sizes instead. That goes against her usual practice, so "Nevertheless" fits. "Likewise" and "Moreover" fail because the Sunshine example is an exception, not something that adds to or matches her usual approach.

Only C says how long the piece will last: 639 years, making it the longest continuous musical performance in history. The other choices name the composer or say where the piece is being played but never give its length.

fix.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• “Organ²/ASLSP (As Slow as Possible)” is a musical piece by avant-garde composer John Cage.
• A specially designed automated organ in St. Burchardi Church in Halberstadt, Germany, began playing the piece in 2001.
• It is scheduled to stop playing the piece in 2640.
• The performance will last 639 years.
• It will be the longest continuous musical performance in history.

choices.A: John Cage is the composer of the musical piece “Organ²/ASLSP (As Slow as Possible).”
choices.B: “Organ²/ASLSP (As Slow as Possible)” is a musical piece currently being played in St. Burchardi Church in Halberstadt, Germany.

explanation: Choice D gives both parts the goal asks for: LIGO's aim (to detect and analyze gravitational waves) and its method (two huge interferometers thousands of miles apart). Choice C describes the method but only mentions "its aims" without saying what they are, and A and B focus on when a wave was detected.

The aim of a study is what the researcher set out to find, and C says Terada "set out to determine" whether some of the Moon's oxygen comes from Earth. Choice D gives the result rather than the aim, and B mentions his question but frames it as something he wondered about rather than the goal of a study.

The notes say Wu is "best known" for her 2011 YouTube video, which has over two million views, and C highlights exactly that. Choices A and B focus on other achievements, and D talks about the composer's work, not Wu.

Choice C does both jobs: it describes the decline (thousands of varieties lost) and explains why it happened (industrial agriculture favored a few varieties suited to commercial growth). Choice B shows the decline but gives no cause, and D talks about crops in general, not apple varieties.

Choice A contrasts where the two words come from: "guerdon" is Anglo-French, while "Laodicean" comes from ancient Greek. Choice B compares the winners but never mentions the words' origins, C gives the origin of only one word, and D groups the words together without showing how they differ.
The goal is to say when al-Biruni published his theory, and only A gives the date: 1037 CE. The other choices describe al-Biruni or his theory but leave out when it was published.

For an audience that doesn't know the book or the author, C explains what Paradise is (a praised historical novel about colonial East Africa) and who Gurnah is (a Nobel Prize winner). Choice A focuses on Gurnah's life rather than the novel, and B and D don't explain who Gurnah is.

The text contrasts the past (before 2009, about 5% of the collection on display) with the present (close to 30% now). "Today" marks this shift to the present. "Nevertheless" fails because the increase is the expected result of the new gallery, not a surprise.

The first sentence says resins play "several important roles," and the next sentences give specific examples: sealing wounds and helping trees hold water. "For example" introduces the first of these. "However" and "Regardless" wrongly signal contrast.

The rocket failed first, and after that the CEO publicly acknowledged the failure and apologized. "Afterward" shows this time order. "Similarly" fails because the CEO's response is not like the failure, and "Indeed" would wrongly suggest that the apology reinforces the previous sentence.

The first sentence says Pleasant successfully challenged discrimination in California, and the second gives the specific details: her 1866 lawsuit against a streetcar company and her win in court. "Specifically" introduces these details. "In addition" fails because the lawsuit isn't a separate point; it is the challenge the first sentence refers to.

The misconception was that the peninsula was an island, and D shows how this mistaken belief led explorers to name it after the fictional island of California. Choices B and C mention the naming but leave out the false belief that the land was an island.

Choice C makes a claim (the predicted shift to large farms may not apply to Thailand) and supports it with evidence from Promkhambut et al.: Thai rice farms modernized while staying small. Choice D makes a similar claim but offers no support, A contradicts the notes, and B is about Asia in general rather than Thailand.

Choice C explains how the bicycles are joined: they share the same rear wheel and face opposite directions. Choice A says that they were fused but not how, and B and D don't describe the joining at all.

The first sentence says the supernovas were likely responsible for forming new stars, and the second explains in detail how: the expanding bubble trapped gas and dust clouds that later collapsed into stars. "Specifically" introduces this more precise explanation. "Hence" fails because the detail is not a result of the first claim; it spells out that claim.

Choice B names an advantage of infilling: it is less invasive than power grinding, which can damage the rock. Choice D mentions that the two methods differ in invasiveness but never says which one is better, so it doesn't present infilling as having an advantage.

Choice A credits Ammal with her success: by crossbreeding imported sugarcane with native grasses, she created hybrids well suited to India's climate. Choices B and C describe the institute's goals rather than what she achieved, and D uses passive voice that leaves Ammal out completely.

Fuller first performed the dance in 1891, and the Lumières filmed it in 1896. "Later" shows that the film came after the first performance. "However" fails because there is no contrast between the two events.

The first sentence says the change was fueled by demand for "certain grains," and the second names those grains (maize and wheat) and explains their role. "In particular" signals this narrowing to specific examples. "By comparison" and "alternatively" wrongly suggest a contrast or an option.

The text describes the steps of making a pot in order: start with the base, build the walls, smooth them, and then paint. "Next" marks the step after the base. "For example" and "By contrast" don't show sequence.

The text follows phytoplankton through time: while alive they absorb carbon, and after they die they sink and store it in seafloor sediment. "Then" marks this next stage. "By contrast" fails because both stages work together to keep carbon out of the atmosphere, so they aren't opposed.
